idiom_name: kotlinx.coroutines: consumer coroutine suspended in Channel.receive() / iterating the channel
implementation_notes: kotlinx.coroutines is Kotlin's de-facto concurrency substrate: a consumer coroutine suspends in Channel.receive() (or iterates the channel with for) and the dispatcher resumes it only when an adapter or producer delivers a message - the asynchronous-receiver property, no thread held while idle, falls out of suspension rather than out of a listener object. What replaces the classic structure is the suspending consumer: instead of registering a MessageListener you launch a coroutine that consumes from an adapter-fed channel (Kafka/AMQP clients are wrapped in a flow or a channel). Keep the classic callback form when a Java library hands you a listener interface you must implement directly.
pitfalls: Bound the channel: an unlimited capacity (Channel.UNLIMITED) lets a fast producer outrun the consumer and grow memory - use a capacity plus suspending send/trySend to signal overload.
The consumer coroutine must be cancelled and awaited at shutdown (structured concurrency); an orphaned consumer keeps the process alive.
An exception in a child consumer coroutine cancels its parent scope - catch per-message failures so one poison message does not tear down the consumer.
consumeEach cancels the underlying channel when it completes; when several consumers share a channel, iterate with for instead.
